source.title: Point of view in personal memories

confidence_rationale: Establishes the core construct MECH-366 needs: personal memories are represented from one of two viewpoints -- FIELD (first-person, original field of view) or OBSERVER (seeing oneself from outside) -- so perspective is a real, represented structural property of an episode, not just an encoding artefact of the camera. That is direct support for the existence of a viewpoint tag. Held at 0.6 (mixed) because the paper does NOT demonstrate the part MECH-366 most needs: that viewpoint is freely SWITCHABLE at retrieval independent of encoding viewpoint. It shows perspective varies with emotion/self-awareness and age of memory, which actually suggests perspective is partly determined by encoding/affect rather than arbitrarily re-set on demand.
failure_signatures: Nigro & Neisser show perspective CORRELATES with emotionality, self-awareness and memory age (older and more self-focused memories drift toward observer perspective). This is evidence that viewpoint is partly DETERMINED by encoding and emotional content, which is in tension with MECH-366's claim that viewpoint is freely switchable at retrieval INDEPENDENT of encoding viewpoint -- the independence is not demonstrated and is mildly contraindicated.

The construct is established by self-report questionnaire on naturalistic memories, with no manipulation showing a single memory can be voluntarily re-experienced from the other viewpoint on demand; switchability is inferred, not tested.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Personal memories are recalled from one of two distinguishable points of view -- 'field' memories, in which the rememberer sees the scene from their original first-person vantage, and 'observer' memories, in which the rememberer sees themselves in the scene from an external vantage. Which perspective dominates varies systematically with emotionality, degree of self-awareness at the time, and the age of the memory.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-366's switchable episodic perspective tag: event tokens carry a viewpoint label (participant/first-person vs observer/third-person). Nigro & Neisser establish that this label is a genuine represented property of autobiographical episodes -- the first half of MECH-366 -- and that it is the same field/observer construct REE names.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Grounds the EXISTENCE of a viewpoint property, NOT its free switchability-at-retrieval-independent-of-encoding (the load-bearing second half of MECH-366). The systematic dependence of perspective on emotion/self-awareness/age that they report actually leans against arbitrary re-setting. Switchability is better evidenced by later work (e.g. voluntary perspective-shift studies); this entry should be read as grounding the construct and flagging switchability as an open follow-up. Human self-report; naturalistic memories.
mapping.source_context: Human cognitive psychology; four studies, recall questionnaires on naturalistic personal memories.

confidence_components.notes: Seminal, well-replicated construct (1983 Cognitive Psychology) -- source quality solid for its era and method (self-report). Mapping fidelity moderate: it nails the construct but not the switchability that distinguishes MECH-366 from a fixed encoding tag. Direction 'mixed' deliberately, not 'supports', because the emotion/age dependence is a mild contra-signal to encoding-independent switching.
